reason: The skin-cell population is already shown in this body's epidermis, with descendants moving toward the surface, so it directly fits the renewal goal.
expectation: The body should show how its skin cells are replaced.

effect: The body now shows skin cells being renewed and shed; I can follow the blood-renewal part next.
reaction: The connection between new basal cells and shedding at the surface is clear.
reason: The picture shows the kidney signal traveling to marrow, where the red-cell precursors are.
expectation: The kidney signal should help the marrow produce red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal is linked to low oxygen and to red-cell maturation in marrow. I should connect the developing cells to the body’s renewal.
reaction: The low-oxygen cue makes the signal’s purpose clearer.
reason: The developing red cells belong to the same body and fit the blood-renewal goal.
expectation: The body should show its red blood cells being renewed alongside its skin.

effect: Skin and blood renewal are complete, and the new goal is to remodel existing bone.
reaction: Seeing red cells leave the marrow connects their development to the blood supply.
reason: The bone-removing and bone-forming cells appear to be the two parts needed to remodel bone, though I don't yet know how the game puts them together.
expectation: The two cell types should begin a bone-remodeling process.

alternatives.reason: I could check what the removing cells can work with first.

effect: The cells did not combine directly; the removing cells acted on the body first, exposing a patch of old bone being removed.
reaction: The compatibility hint made the order clearer.
reason: The remaining bone-forming cells suggest the next step is to rebuild the patch after old bone is removed.
expectation: Bone-forming cells should add new bone to the remodeling patch.

effect: Bone-forming cells rebuilt the patch after old bone was removed, completing the renewal goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the earlier arm still moving while the body’s tissues renew.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the kidney signal to developing red cells was worthwhile because the low-oxygen cue explained why the body adjusts red-cell production.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the skin-cell population to the body was straightforward, but mostly confirmed the renewal already shown in its picture.

surprise.text: The bone-removing and bone-forming cells could not combine directly; the removing cells had to act on the body first.

arbitrary.text: The exact bone-remodeling order was not clear to me before the compatibility hint, although removing old bone before rebuilding it made sense afterward.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter connected familiar body functions in a similarly clear way. The low-oxygen signal and bone renewal gave me a reason to see how the pieces fit.
